title: protobuf request parsing: a JSON body that spells one field both snake_case and camelCase is rejected with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE before parse_dict
answers: Why does my gateway secret update return 400 saying the request specifies both 'secret_id' and 'secretId'?
A client sent both snake_case and camelCase keys for the same field in a tracking or registry request; why is it rejected now?
Where is the check that stops duplicate field spellings in REST request bodies?
Does a workspace create or update body that carries both default_artifact_root and defaultArtifactRoot get rejected?
Why are map-field keys and google.protobuf well-known fields exempt from the alias-conflict check?
body:
Path: Every proto-backed REST request body parsed by mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_request_message (tracking, model registry, gateway and other ajax endpoints), plus workspace create/update bodies parsed by mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_workspace_request_message. The chokepoint is mlflow/server/handlers.py:_reject_conflicting_field_aliases, which runs on the raw JSON before parse_dict.
Rule: If a message field and its json_name both appear as keys in the same object, reject with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE. The check recurses into nested non-map message fields, including each item of a repeated list (for example model_configs). Map entries and google.protobuf.* types are skipped because their keys are caller-chosen. Any new body parser must call _reject_conflicting_field_aliases before parse_dict, or go through _get_request_message.
Symptom: ParseDict accepts both spellings and the later key wins, while basic-auth validators read the raw snake_case key. A user with READ on one gateway secret could send secret_id for their own secret and secretId for another, so authorization checked one secret and the handler updated the other (GHSA-3g8m-hm3x-gh2r).
Constraints: Applies to request bodies only, not query parameters read by _get_request_param. A body with only one spelling, in either form, is accepted. Applies whether or not the basic-auth app is mounted, since the handler-side guard protects every deployment.
applies: Any proto-backed REST request body in mlflow/server/handlers.py, in every app, including workspace create and update.
says: Updating a gateway secret returns an invalid parameter error about duplicate keys.
Creating a workspace fails when submitting both naming styles for default artifact storage.
Tracking and model registry requests fail when payload contains conflicting field name aliases.
Why does updating a secret return an error about specifying the same property twice?
search: Proto-backed REST request bodies parsed in mlflow/server/handlers.py via _get_request_message or _get_workspace_request_message are checked by _reject_conflicting_field_aliases before parse_dict to reject with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE if a message field and its json_name both appear in the same JSON object. The validation recurses into nested non-map message fields and repeated lists such as model_configs, but skips map entries and google.protobuf.* types. The guard applies to tracking, model registry, gateway, and workspace create or update bodies regardless of basic-auth mounting, but does not apply to query parameters parsed by _get_request_param or bodies containing only one spelling.
